business_rules.title: Active membership definition
business_rules.description: Membership is active if status is active, remaining_lessons > 0 and end_date >= today.
business_rules.condition: status == active AND remaining_lessons > 0 AND end_date >= date.today()

business_rules.title: Expired membership refresh
business_rules.description: Active membership with end_date before today is changed to expired during serialization/lookup.

business_rules.title: Membership finishes at zero lessons
business_rules.description: Write-off or update sets membership to finished when remaining lessons reaches zero.

business_rules.title: Returning visit restores lesson
business_rules.description: Cancelling a visit increments remaining lessons and restores status to active if not expired and previously finished.
business_rules.result: visit.is_cancelled = true; membership.remaining_lessons += 1; status expired or active

business_rules.title: Course creates four weekly events
business_rules.description: If event_type is course and recurrence is absent, backend sets weekly count=4.

business_rules.title: Schedule time is 30-minute grid
business_rules.description: Start/end minutes must be 0 or 30, no seconds/microseconds, duration >= 30 and multiple of 30.

business_rules.title: Completion writes visits
business_rules.description: Completing scheduled event creates Visit for attended participants and decrements their active membership.
business_rules.result: create Visit; link visit_id; event completed

business_rules.title: Cancelling completed event returns visits
business_rules.description: Cancelling a completed event cancels each linked active visit and marks attendance cancelled.
business_rules.result: linked visits cancelled; lessons returned; event cancelled

business_rules.title: Practice is independent of Visit
business_rules.description: Practice rentals create PracticeRental only and contribute to finance as practice income.

business_rules.title: Active extra expenses enter finance
business_rules.description: get_extra_expenses_total filters active extra expenses by date range.

business_rules.title: MonthlyExpense is payment obligation source
business_rules.description: Payment obligation DTO is derived from MonthlyExpense and ExpenseCategory; no separate table exists.

business_rules.title: Variable obligations require actual amount
business_rules.description: Variable non-teacher expenses cannot be paid until actual_amount exists or is provided.
business_rules.condition: category.is_variable and not teacher expense and actual_amount absent

business_rules.title: Operator has no finance.view
business_rules.description: Operator lacks finance permissions and /finance route is hidden/blocked.
business_rules.result: 403 for finance API; no Finance nav item

technical_debt.title: No repository/data access layer
technical_debt.description: Routers and services access SQLAlchemy Session directly. This keeps MVP simple but makes impact analysis and transaction ownership harder.
technical_debt.recommendation: Introduce repositories only when query duplication or transaction boundaries become painful.

technical_debt.title: Duplicate dashboard endpoint
technical_debt.description: /dashboard and /finance/dashboard return similar dashboard data with different permissions.
technical_debt.recommendation: Deprecate /finance/dashboard after frontend no longer references it.

technical_debt.title: Read endpoints can write data
technical_debt.description: Finance report and list endpoints ensure monthly expenses and backfill visit financial fields during reads.
technical_debt.recommendation: Separate idempotent maintenance jobs from read-model generation.

technical_debt.title: Legacy Payment entity remains in code
technical_debt.description: Payment model exists although recent finance logic is lesson-based and mandatory-payment-based. No active payments router was found in current OpenAPI.
technical_debt.recommendation: Decide whether Payment is deprecated, archival, or should return as a supported module.

technical_debt.title: Frontend guards are role-based, backend has permissions
technical_debt.description: Frontend RoleRoute uses roles arrays while backend has a permission enum for finance/payment obligations.
technical_debt.recommendation: Expose effective permissions in /auth/me and guard UI by permissions.

technical_debt.title: Mutations often commit before audit log
technical_debt.description: Services commit domain changes; routers then log audit in a separate commit path. Audit can be missed if log write fails after domain commit.
technical_debt.recommendation: Wrap domain mutation and audit write in one transaction boundary.

technical_debt.title: Naive datetime.utcnow usage
technical_debt.description: Models and services use datetime.utcnow, which produces naive datetimes and emitted deprecation warnings during tests.
technical_debt.recommendation: Move to timezone-aware UTC datetimes consistently.

technical_debt.title: Possible N+1 in list/serialization code
technical_debt.description: Some endpoints serialize ORM objects with relationship access after ad-hoc queries. Several queries use joinedload, but the pattern is not systematic.
technical_debt.recommendation: Benchmark with real data and standardize eager loading per response DTO.

technical_debt.title: Manual local migrations in startup
technical_debt.description: Schema changes are handled with inspect/alter table logic in app startup instead of versioned migrations.
technical_debt.recommendation: Adopt Alembic before multi-environment production growth.

open_questions.question: Is the Payment model intentionally deprecated or should it remain part of product finance?
open_questions.reason: Payment model exists, but current finance page removed received-payments emphasis and no payments router appears in current OpenAPI.

open_questions.question: Should role=finance see practice and extra-expenses operational pages?
open_questions.reason: Frontend routes expose practice/extra-expenses to finance role; backend permits authenticated reads for those endpoints, but business wording primarily separates finance analytics from operator obligations.

open_questions.question: Should operators be allowed to physically delete schedule events?
open_questions.reason: Current backend uses require_operator_access for DELETE /schedule-events/{event_id}, while practice/extra-expense physical deletes are admin-only.

open_questions.question: Should dashboard expose finance summary values to operator?
open_questions.reason: /dashboard is authenticated for all roles and returns school earnings values, while /finance is denied for operator.
